# CP/M 2.2 provenance and SHINO-80 port delta

- Source repository: <https://github.com/brouhaha/cpm22>
- Source commit: `01018abbccce0bdf4874b0b2ed1a048c5fcc2987`
- Imported upstream SHA-256:
  - `ccp.asm`: `015dc575a8e4d8d54057a7d014b90cf17df490c0e356346cc740cb0d3a73d262`
  - `bdos.asm`: `2f715ad338278d5b7c63546492ae1b25b2871ab7d42a70cc2b90ff8aa0f52930`
  - `LICENSE.txt`: `a9bcdbc66bb31b86882e84469f133b3bd5598f46423b4c6bbb6bedb9f2eac754`
- Repository text snapshots use normalized line endings. Their current hashes:
  - `ccp.asm`: `497aea556887cbae6f2fc54f24b9826fcd17950f1534f9e54d9b67de094949bc`
  - ported `bdos.asm`: `76655d6a1e2754f98b929fe1c16713acb633f8a5aa777f5d7ff21be76783a4e4`
- Assembler: Macroassembler AS
  <https://github.com/Macroassembler-AS/asl-releases>, commit
  `c7155b4fd3d33110f0eb098dede4295a8c008772`.

44K origins are retained: CCP `9400h`, BDOS `9C00h`. One deliberate port delta
exists in `bdos.asm`: the upstream expression that places BIOS immediately
after BDOS (`AA00h`) is replaced by the SHINO-80 RAM CBIOS base `FA00h`.
This keeps the TPA below CCP while allowing SHINO-80's memory-mapped display and
high-memory firmware ABI to remain original. CCP is otherwise unmodified.

Rebuild commands:

```sh
asl -D origin=9400h -o ccp-44k.p -L -OLIST ccp-44k.lst ccp.asm
p2bin -l '$00' -r '$9400-$9bff' ccp-44k.p
asl -D origin=9c00h -o bdos-shino80-44k.p -L -OLIST bdos-shino80-44k.lst bdos.asm
p2bin -l '$00' -r '$9c00-$a9ff' bdos-shino80-44k.p
```

The generated bytes are embedded in `src/firmware/shino80/shino80-cpm22.js`.
Its length and SHA-256 constants are tested against the reconstructed images.
